items.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney tells DW that Canada is seeking closer EU ties to "diversify and deepen" partnerships beyond the Americas. Despite German pushback, he said he favors the all-new term "associate membership."

items.title: Ukraine: Oleshky residents evacuate war-ravaged city
items.summary: Under the local ceasefire, an aid convoy of 25 buses arrived with humanitarian aid and as transport for fleeing Oleshky residents. The Ukrainian city has been occupied by Russia since 2022 and faces food shortages.

items.title: Smuggling, power, profit: Irregular migration out of eastern Libya
items.summary: There is currently more irregular migration between eastern Libya and Crete, Greece. It's raising questions as to what connects people smugglers with powerful militias in eastern Libya and then in turn, Europeans.

items.title: Tennessee woman Christa Pike describes pain after failed execution
items.summary: Christa Pike says she remains in constant pain a month after surviving a lethal injection in Tennessee. Her lawyers want her death sentence reduced to life, while the state governor has ordered an investigation.

items.title: What the rift within the Tsikhanouski family means for the Belarusian opposition in exile
items.summary: Siarhei Tsikhanouski criticizes the work of his wife, Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, and her office. He also questions her legitimacy. What are the implications for Belarusian political forces in exile?

items.title: US midterms: Pope Leo XIV casts vote by mail
items.summary: As a US citizen, Pope Leo XIV is eligible to vote in US elections and has made use of that right with a postal ballot ahead of Tuesday's midterms. The pontiff, a Chicago native, did not reveal who he voted for.

items.title: Binance crypto exchange suspends trades over North Korea-linked hack
items.summary: Crypto platform Binance has suspended trading following a suspected hack now linked to North Korea. The disruption has left users unable to trade on the cryptocurrency platform while the suspected breach is investigated.

items.title: Germany news: Merz hopes for Korean reunification at DMZ
items.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz has expressed hope for Korean reunification during a visit to the heavily fortified border. Meanwhile, President Steinmeier has held talks with China's Xi Jinping in Beijing. DW has more.

items.title: Seoul fears being sidelined as US reaches out to North Korea
items.summary: With ties between South Korea and the Trump administration strained, the South Korean government worries that Donald Trump's pursuit of a diplomatic breakthrough with Kim Jong Un may come at Seoul's expense.

items.title: Bollywood and the underworld — together in the spotlight?
items.summary: A wave of shootings and extortion threats has rattled India's film industry. This time, those claiming responsibility are very different from the Mumbai underworld that had Bollywood in its grip back in the 1990s.

items.title: Bayern Munich's Kenya friendly highlights Africa's growing pull for global sport
items.summary: Bayern Munich are to open Nairobi's new Raila Odinga International Stadium against Ajax as Kenya prepares for AFCON 2027. The match highlights Africa's growing sports ambitions — and questions over cost and legacy.

items.title: Italy: Students and workers rally over living costs
items.summary: Students and workers have marched across Italy for more school funding and relief from rising living costs. The rallies follow weeks of school occupations and protests against higher military spending.

items.title: Germany takes cautious approach on Israeli election results
items.summary: German politicians have been slow to respond as they wait to see who is likely to comprise the next coalition. Many are also hoping for a government without religious hardliners.

items.title: Russia: Critical newspaper 'Novaya Gazeta' to close
items.summary: "Novaya Gazeta," one of the last remaining independent, critical media outlets in Russia, has announced it is closing under pressure from state authorities. Meanwhile, in Ukraine, evacuations have begun in Oleshky.

items.title: Brazil's new anti-gang law: Can it curb organized crime?
items.summary: A tough stance against organized crime? One year after a massacre that left more than 130 people dead, a new law aims to crack down on drug cartels in Rio's favelas.

items.title: IIHF ordered to allow Russia back into world championships
items.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has ruled that Russian teams must be allowed to take part in international ice hockey tournaments. The IIHF had banned Russia following the country's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

items.title: Many Turkish 'guest workers' hit by poverty in old age
items.summary: West Germany and Turkey signed an agreement allowing the temporary recruitment of workers on October 30, 1961. Sixty-five years on, many so-called 'guest workers' can't live from their pensions.

items.title: The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism
items.summary: From Picasso to Andy Warhol, a surprising number of artists have portrayed the German breed. But the dachshund has also at times been co-opted as a political symbol.

items.title: India news: Space agency to boost GPS alternative with new satellite
items.summary: The Indian national space agency's mission aims to strengthen its indigenous navigation system and reduce reliance on the US-owned GPS. Meanwhile, Rahul Gandhi renewed his call for more election protests. DW has more.

items.title: Israeli election: Netanyahu, main rival fall short of majority after all votes counted
items.summary: With all the votes counted, the pro-Netanyahu bloc finished ahead of Gadi Eisenkot's anti-Netanyahu bloc. But tough coalition talks loom as neither grouping won a majority. DW has more.

items.title: Germany's Alexander Zverev clinches tennis No. 1 ranking
items.summary: Alexander Zverev is the second German man, after Boris Becker, to clinch the No. 1 spot in tennis.

items.title: 'Star Trek' star Patrick Stewart dies age 86
items.summary: The Shakespearean actor landed the role of a lifetime as "Star Trek" Captain Picard. He passed away at age 86.

items.title: India increases growth forecast for fiscal year
items.summary: India's Ministry of Finance has increased its growth forecasts for the current fiscal year. But it also warned about inflation, particularly for fuel and energy, amid continued instability in the Middle East.

items.title: Germany seeks new head of state
items.summary: The question of who should become Germany's new presiden is becoming pressing. Many want to see Germany's first female head of state. Chancellor Friedrich Merz is keeping his cards close to his chest.

items.title: Volkswagen logs Q3 operating loss of €5.86 billion on Porsche writedown
items.summary: The Volkswagen Group has filed its worst quarterly performance since the height of the "Dieselgate" scandal in 2015. Share prices climbed in response, however, perhaps because the bad news was so well signposted.

items.title: Russia shadow fleet sanctions: Can the EU act without US?
items.summary: The US is reportedly considering ways to convert "dark tankers" into legitimate vessels, allowing them to transport crude oil that is not subject to sanctions.

items.title: Germany news: Chancellor Friedrich Merz accuses North Korea of threatening Europe's freedom
items.summary: Friedrich Merz, who is visiting Seoul, said North Korea is putting Europe's security at risk by sending soldiers to fight for Russia in Ukraine. DW has more.

items.title: European Central Bank (ECB) head Christine Lagarde to step down in February, before her term ends
items.summary: European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde is to resign nine months ahead of the end of her 8-year term. European Council President Antonio Costa has said the process to find a successor is underway.

items.title: Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany's health scare highlights the need for better support for elite coaches
items.summary: Vincent Kompany’s health concern is a reminder that elite football's pressures affect coaches too. Better support, clearer structures and mental health safeguards are increasingly vital.

items.title: Evacuation from Oleshky: How are preparations going?
items.summary: A lawyer with the Save Ukraine Foundation, Myroslava Kharchenko, told DW about what has been happening in Russian-occupied Oleshky since a temporary ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump took effect.

items.title: Gen Z protests in Germany: Is France-style violence looming?
items.summary: Young people in Germany are preparing to protest over education and climate change. Politicians fear violence like in France, but an expert sees differences.

items.title: Can we regrow damaged seagrass meadows?
items.summary: Seagrass protects coasts, shelters thousands of species and stores CO2. But some 30% of this valuable ecosystem has disappeared since the late 19th century. Can we bring it back?

items.title: EU's 'Made in Europe' push unnerves global auto suppliers
items.summary: In shielding Europe's carmakers from Chinese rivals, the EU risks hurting close partners from Turkey and Morocco to Japan and South Korea. Billions in trade and hundreds of thousands of European jobs are at stake.

items.title: Russia in Africa: What is Putin hoping to achieve?
items.summary: Following its invasion of Ukraine and the resulting rift with the West, Russia has declared that it intends to make a "historic return" to Africa. What have we seen of this so far?

items.title: Africa's first Youth Olympics open in Senegal amid hope and scrutiny
items.summary: Senegal is hosting Africa's first Youth Olympics, with 2,700 young athletes competing in Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly. The Games bring pride and hope, but also questions over cost, rights and legacy.

items.title: Serbian police shoot dead assailant at Israeli Embassy
items.summary: A "minor" has been killed by police after attacking a guard at Israel's embassy in Belgrade with knives, the interior minister says. Ivica Dacic said police had declared the highest terror alert after the incident.

items.title: Harry Kane: Ballon d’Or for Bayern Munich striker
items.summary: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane has won football's most prestigious individual prize, beating Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal. Kane has developed even more in the Bundesliga despite an uneven league.

items.title: Germany's Merz says erosion of global order means middle powers in Europe and Asia must be more assertive
items.summary: During a visit to Singapore, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Europe and Germany want to increase free trade with open competition, reliability and a rules-based order.

items.title: England and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or
items.summary: The England captain ends his country's 25-year wait for the prestigious award after scoring 73 goals for club and country last season, beating competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.

items.title: Steinmeier in China: A major state visit in uncertain times
items.summary: President Frank-Walter Steinmeier is traveling to China on a state visit in a period of political and economic uncertainty. Germany is seeking alternative partners in the region but also wants good ties with Beijing.

items.title: From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated
items.summary: Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes. But ahead of the US midterm elections, does disgust shape our politics, or do our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?

items.title: France: Hundreds arrested after nationwide protests
items.summary: The French government says more than 1,000 people were arrested following nationwide protests on Saturday. Police and elite security forces were out in force across the country as clashes broke out.

items.title: Prague honors Roma resistance fighters against Hitler
items.summary: More than 1,400 Roma fought against the German Nazi occupation in Czechoslovakia. A new exhibition in Prague showcases the stories of partisans and soldiers whose fates barely received any attention for decades.

items.title: In Bulgaria, record low voter turnout triggers a November 1 presidential run-off in a poll colored by divisions over Ukraine war
items.summary: Low voter turnout has triggered a run-off for the Bulgarian presidency. The vote was colored by strong divisions over Russia's war in Ukraine, and Sofia's relations with the Kremlin.

items.title: Turkey's new deal on Mediterranean maritime boundaries with Libya is exacerbating issues with Greece and the EU
items.summary: Turkey and Libya plan to redraw maritime boundaries in the Mediterranean as part of a new economic corridor. This has sparked strong protests from Greece, and has also drawn the European Union into the conflict.

items.title: EU moves to loosen rules on pesticide use as experts sound the alarm
items.summary: The European Union wants to relax rules for pesticides, saying it will be easier for farmers to adopt more environmentally friendly options. But health and environmental experts say the risks are far too great.

items.title: Russia's attacks on Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, are intensifying. DW asked people on the ground what life is like

items.title: Serbia: Hope, tension and apprehension as voters prepare to elect new parliament

items.title: Germany sit out FIFA Under-15 World Cup as Russia return

items.title: Albania's student protests are only getting bigger

items.title: Are the French police the most violent in the EU?
items.summary: As protests continue in France, the French police are under scrutiny after new allegations of police brutality. The force has a bigger arsenal than most in Europe.

items.title: Ukraine: Life near the front line in Sloviansk
items.summary: As Russian continues to attack Sloviansk in eastern Ukraine, thousands of residents refuse to leave or struggle to find a way out. For many, poverty, family ties and beloved pets make evacuation painfully difficult.

items.title: Can Germany revive its economy before the far-right AfD gains ground?

items.title: Bulgaria: Concerns about security in the Black Sea dominate presidential election campaign

items.summary: Far-right Alternative for Germany co-leader Alice Weidel reveals the party's plan to reform the EU. Meanwhile, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was in Berlin to talk to developers and investors. DW has more.

items.summary: Russian FSB agents have arrested a German national and accused him of fighting as a mercenary for Ukraine's military. They claim he deserted over unpaid wages and say he was a sniper who once served in the Bundeswehr.

items.title: US sanctions target Iran's rail sector as Tehran shifts cargo from sea routes to overland corridors
items.summary: As US sanctions expand to Iran's rail sector, Tehran is relying more heavily on overland links with China and Central Asia. But capacity constraints, delays and costs limit rail's ability to replace maritime trade.

items.title: Football: German coach Hürzeler flying high in Premier League
items.summary: Fabian Hürzeler is younger than his star player, a fellow Premier League German. But, contrary to his reputation in his homeland, Hürzeler has become a popular figure both on and off the pitch in England.

items.title: Rising emissions and temperatures: The cost of Trump's climate retreat is now clear
items.summary: The world is set to breach the critical 1.5-degree temperature limit, with Donald Trump's US withdrawal from climate action worsening the outlook, according to a UN report. But there is a small silver lining.

items.title: Germany news: Hackers release AfD party emails
items.summary: Germany's far-right AfD has launched an inquiry after the release of thousands of emails following a cyberattack. Also, investors pledged billions for Germany at a major summit in Berlin. DW has more news from Germany.

items.title: Wagner brothers begin new NBA chapter on different paths
items.summary: After five years, brothers Franz and Moritz Wagner are no longer playing together for the Orlando Magic. In the new NBA season, their separation will likely mean the new "German" team is the Charlotte Hornets.

items.title: Why US investors are snapping up Germany's famed Mittelstand
items.summary: Increasing amounts of US capital are flowing into Germany's traditional industrial firms and family-owned businesses. As many business owners struggle to find successors, more companies are becoming acquisition targets.

items.title: Brutal, revolutionary empire builder: Genghis Khan's legacy
items.summary: Berlin is host to a major exhibition on the founder of the Mongol Empire and his successors. Here's how Genghis Khan disrupted the course of history.

items.title: Bulgaria seeks suspects in Germany after Starlink sabotage
items.summary: A Bulgarian court has issued arrest warrants for two young German nationals suspected of setting fire to Starlink antennas. The case is reminiscent of another in Poland, which Warsaw says was orchestrated by Russia.

items.title: Germany news: Emergency at Leipzig airport sparked by novice driver
items.summary: Two men breached a fence at the Leipzig/Halle airport while practicing for a driving test. Meanwhile, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced an industrial AI partnership with Nvidia. DW has more.

items.title: The homeless man living in front of a London mega-mansion
items.summary: Anders Fernstedt lives in London without any money. The Swedish native has built a most unusual home under the porch of a house worth over €200 million. How did that happen?

items.title: Is Germany's eight-hour workday under threat?
items.summary: Would you work 12 hours straight? The CDU/CSU and SPD are locked in a dispute over reforms to the Working Hours Act. Workplace flexibility, collective bargaining agreements and worker protection rules are at stake.

items.title: How big is Russia's threat against Germany?
items.summary: Experts believe that, so far, Germany has been ill-prepared — both militarily and mentally — for Russian provocations. They also warn against the idea that ending support for Ukraine would make Germany safer.

items.title: China's influence in the gaming industry is growing
items.summary: Home to more than 700 million gamers, China is the world's largest gaming market — but it's also one of the most tightly regulated. The effects reach far beyond China, impacting players around the world.

items.title: The Bundestag has debated the genocide Germany carried out in Namibia a century ago. But will it spur progress on addressing colonial crimes?
items.summary: Opposition parties have forced a debate in the Bundestag on the early-20th-century genocide Germany carried out in Namibia. Will this finally spur progress in addressing colonial crimes?

items.summary: She started taking action against Hitler as a teenager and never stopped until her death in a concentration camp. Berlin's Blücherplatz is now being renamed after her.

items.title: EU promotes sovereign, trusted AI as it struggles to catch US and China
items.summary: At an international AI summit in Dublin, EU leaders promoted trusted and independent artificial intelligence. Critics question whether the bloc can close the gap with the US and China while maintaining strict regulation.

items.title: Formula One in Rwanda: Sportswashing claims vs. hopes for African legacy

items.title: Resignation of Bärbel Bas shines light on harsh era of German politics
items.summary: German Labor Minister Bärbel Bas has stepped down, citing her need to grieve a loved one and leave behind the harsh realities of government. So how did German politics get so heated?

items.title: AI-assisted dying? Doris Dörrie's new film addresses prospect of care robots
items.summary: While the world debates the dangers of artificial intelligence, filmmaker Doris Dörrie explores how humanoid robots could change the way we deal with aging, caregiving and how people choose to die.

items.title: Thousands of German gamblers could sue for their money back
items.summary: German gamblers may finally be able to beat the house, thanks to new court rulings in the EU and in Germany. The decisions could help gambling addicts — but the legal road might be difficult.

items.title: Germany news: Train station alcohol ban comes into force
items.summary: Consuming alcohol is no longer permitted at train stations in Germany, to improve the lot of travelers and staff alike. Coalition talks are restarting in Berlin, and an inmate is loose in Essen.

items.title: Brazil's elections matter for the planet. This is why
items.summary: Brazil is heading back to the polls, but the impact could be felt worldwide. With the Amazon vital to the health of the planet, the election could help shape its future.

items.title: Why Chinese tech brands are outpacing Western rivals from EVs to robot vacuums
items.summary: From action cameras and smartphones to EVs and robot vacuums, Chinese brands are gaining ground worldwide, despite privacy and security concerns. What's driving their rise, and can European rivals keep up?

items.title: Manchester City, the UAE and the UK's OM in a political tangle
items.summary: Nearly 20 years after arriving in England, Manchester City's UAE owners could exit amid cheating charges. That would pose a challenge for a city — and prime minister — closely tied to Abu Dhabi.

items.title: Nord Stream trial opens in Germany, defense seeks dismissal
items.summary: Serhii Kuznietsov is accused of attacking civilian infrastructure in the 2022 sabotage of the Russian gas pipeline to Germany. His lawyers called Nord Stream a military target, and said their client is sworn to secrecy.

items.title: Trump's diesel deal with Russia is unlikely to significantly lower global fuel prices despite expectations of rapid relief
items.summary: As the world's largest diesel exporter, the US benefits from high prices. At home, however, consumers are feeling the strain of rising living costs. Why Donald Trump's deal with Russia is unlikely to change that.

items.title: FIFPRO report highlights growing pains in women's football
items.summary: Expected global revenue of over $1 billion and new faces at the U17 World Cup show women's football is booming, but a recent report also highlights need for better structures globally.

items.title: The hidden treasure in discarded wearable and fast tech
items.summary: Sales of fast tech like mini fans and disposable e-vapes, as well as wearable health tech such as heart monitors and smartwatches are soaring. They're creating a new e-waste problem but are full of hidden treasure.

items.title: Formula 1: Rwanda to bring sport back to Africa
items.summary: The last time Formula 1 hosted a race in Africa was way back in 1993. But a new track in Rwanda is set to host a Grand Prix in "the early 2030s," continuing the country’s investment in international sport.

items.title: Germany's China calculation shifts as import pressures eclipse export benefits
items.summary: Germany has long resisted tougher action against China, fearing retaliation. But rising pressure on key industries has pushed Berlin to seek stronger EU trade-defense powers to protect its industrial base.

items.title: 125 years of Thomas Mann's 'Buddenbrooks'

items.title: Pope lung nodule: Could it be cancer?
items.summary: The case of Pope Leo shows how small lung nodules are often found during routine health checks. Quick treatment is generally advised before nodules can grow to become larger life-threatening masses.

items.title: Germany's women: Ena Mahmutovic makes her case to become Germany's next No.1 goalkeeper
items.summary: Germany's win against Australia saw Ena Mahmutovic excel in goal. The 22-year-old Bayern Munich goalkeeper is considered the successor to Ann-Katrin Berger and is making a name for herself.

items.title: How green is Europe's urban public transport? A data-driven reality check

items.title: UK students call for school uniforms to be banned in pornography
items.summary: Short skirts, knee-high socks, white blouses: Girls' school uniform items are widely used as costumes in pornographic videos. As students experience harassment, a group wants to change that.

items.title: 'Ragebait' is the 2026 German Youth Word of the Year
items.summary: Already named the 2025 Oxford Word of the Year, "rage bait" has also been widely adopted in German slang.

items.title: Author or artificial intelligence? Literature in crisis
items.summary: AI is a hot topic at this year's Frankfurt Book Fair. An international literary scandal has raised questions about machine-generated texts.

items.title: Art for freedom: Maria Kalesnikava in Bonn

items.title: World Cup 2034: Does Saudi Arabia shelving Neom Stadium spell trouble?
items.summary: Since winning the right to hold the 2034 World Cup unopposed, Saudi Arabia has been pulling away from sport. With reports that its most ambitious stadium project will be abandoned, what does this mean for the World Cup?

items.title: Finland, the world's happiest nation, faces a glum winter
